messages.subject: Sampling from the posterior distribution in INLA
parts:
Hi, I have fitted a geostatistical model with two covariates when one covariate is categorical, see the summary:

```
summary(mod)
Time used:
    Pre = 2.25, Running = 159, Post = 4.59, Total = 165
Fixed effects:
           mean     sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant    mode kld
b0      -56.093 36.805   -141.594  -46.515     -2.609 -39.819   0
x1        0.313  0.122      0.079    0.316      0.535   0.370   0
x2< 50  -29.355 26.915    -83.310  -28.837     21.954 -28.822   0
x2>= 80 -59.141 35.203   -120.782  -61.932      6.161 -76.357   0
x250-60  32.610 34.084    -13.145   22.683    111.348  16.413   0
x260-70  30.414 33.649    -15.005   20.575    107.225  14.296   0
x270-80  32.603 33.966    -13.902   22.810    109.629  16.508   0

Random effects:
  Name   Model
    s SPDE2 model
   rr IID model

Model hyperparameters:
                   mean     sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant   mode
Range for s      39.552 11.722     21.307   37.958      67.03 34.981
Stdev for s       1.449  0.231      1.048    1.431       1.95  1.397
Precision for rr  0.927  0.435      0.382    0.831       2.05  0.672

```
After sampling from the posterior distribution, how do I deal with the categorical nature of the x2 variable when creating the linear predictor. Should I create the dummy variables for my categorical variable? I'm using the code below to extract the required information from the posterior samples

```
nsamp <- 1000

#Posterior sampling
ps <- inla.posterior.sample(nsamp, mod, num.threads = 7, parallel.configs = T)
contents <- mod$misc$configs$contents

#ID for spatial random effect
idSpace <- contents$start[which(contents$tag=="s")]-1 +
  (1:contents$length[which(contents$tag=="s")])

#ID for iid effects/noise
idR <- contents$start[which(contents$tag=="rr")]-1 +
  (1:contents$length[which(contents$tag=="rr")])


#ID for fixed effects
    pred$soil_pH_cat <- as.factor(pred$soil_pH_cat)
    x2 <- model.matrix(~ pred$soil_pH_cat - 1)
idX <- contents$start[which(contents$tag=="b0")]-1 + (1:(2 + ncol(x2)))

# extract samples
xLatent <- matrix(0, nrow=length(ps[[1]]$latent), ncol=nsamp)
xHyper <- matrix(0, nrow=length(ps[[1]]$hyperpar), ncol=nsamp)

for(i in 1:nsamp) {
  xLatent[,i] <- ps[[i]]$latent
  xHyper[,i] <- ps[[i]]$hyperpar
}
xSpace <- xLatent[idSpace,]
XR <- xLatent[idR,]
xX <- xLatent[idX,]

#Prediction
#Draw samples for IID term
sample.IIDpred <- matrix(0, nrow(pred),  nsamp)
for (i in 1:nsamp) {
  ID.precision <- xHyper[3,i] #the 3rd row contains precision for rr; same as ps[[i]]$hyperpar[3]
  ID.sigma <- ID.precision^-0.5
  sample.IIDpred[, i] <- rnorm(nrow(pred), sd = ID.sigma)
}

x1 = pred$lst_day
pred$soil_pH_cat <- as.factor(pred$soil_pH_cat)
x2 <- model.matrix(~ pred$soil_pH_cat - 1)

linpred <-
  as.matrix(Ap %*% xSpace + as.matrix(
    cbind(
      1,
      x1,
      x2
    )
  ) %*% xX + sample.IIDpred)

inv.linpred <- gtools::inv.logit(linpred)

```

parts:
I would use the inla.posterior.sample.eval() function to extract these. Note
that the linear predictor is already there as 'Predictor' or 'APredictor'

there is a vignette about this, which I think you'll find useful.

like

inla.posterior.sample.eval("x2< 50", ps)

would extract these, etc.

Dear Havard,

Thank you for your answer, I understand that I can easily obtain the posterior samples of my categorical variables (and any other estimate) by using inla.posterior.sample.eval. However, I am using these posterior Samples of the regression coefficients, random noise, matrix index A and spatial random effect to multiply with the matrix of covariates from my prediction data set to obtain the linear predictor. Is creating dummy variables for categorical predictors in the prediction dataset the correct approach for matrix conformity, especially when applying the posterior samples to the covariates from the prediction data to compute the linear predictor?

Also, I have learnt the linear predictor is already constructed, first, I have both the APredictor and Predictor in my contents
```

$length

 Which of this should I use and what's the difference between them?

Finally, suppose that I use "Predictor" as my linear predictor;

```
linpred_samples <- inla.posterior.sample.eval("Predictor", ps)
dim(linpred_samples)
[1] 24691  1000

```
How do I proceed from here? My guess is I should multiply the linear predictor with the matrix of my covariates from the prediction data, however, the matrices are not conformable

parts:
if you use control.predictor=list(A=...) then you have lin.pred in two layers

data depends on eta*

eta* = A %*% eta

eta is defined in the formula

then

APredictor = eta*

Predictor = eta

if 'A' is not used, then APredictor is NULL



What exactly do you want to do??? Normally, building the lin.predictor
'yourself' is not needed.

Here x1, x2, x3, x4 are categorical

```
formula <- y ~ 0 + b0 + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 +
  f(s, model = spde) +
  f(rr, model = 'iid', hyper = hyper.prec)

#' The inla() call
mod <- inla(
  formula,
  family = "binomial",
  Ntrials = numtrials,
  data = inla.stack.data(stk.full),

    compute = TRUE,
    link = 1,
    A = inla.stack.A(stk.full)
  ),

  control.inla = list(tolerance = 1e-7),
  num.threads = 7,
  verbose = F
)

nsamp <- 1000

#Posterior sampling
ps <- inla.posterior.sample(nsamp, mod, num.threads = 7, parallel.configs = T)
contents <- mod$misc$configs$contents

#ID for spatial random effect
idSpace <- contents$start[which(contents$tag=="s")]-1 +
  (1:contents$length[which(contents$tag=="s")])

#ID for iid effects/noise
idR <- contents$start[which(contents$tag=="rr")]-1 +
  (1:contents$length[which(contents$tag=="rr")])

#ID for fixed effects
idX <- contents$start[which(contents$tag=="b0")]-1 + (1:(2 + ncol(pred_dummy)))

# extract samples
xLatent <- matrix(0, nrow=length(ps[[1]]$latent), ncol=nsamp)
xHyper <- matrix(0, nrow=length(ps[[1]]$hyperpar), ncol=nsamp)

for(i in 1:nsamp) {
  xLatent[,i] <- ps[[i]]$latent
  xHyper[,i] <- ps[[i]]$hyperpar
}
xSpace <- xLatent[idSpace,]
XR <- xLatent[idR,]
xX <- xLatent[idX,]

#Prediction
#Draw samples for IID term
sample.IIDpred <- matrix(0, nrow(pred),  nsamp)
for (i in 1:nsamp) {
  ID.precision <- xHyper[3,i] #the 3rd row contains precision for rr; same as ps[[i]]$hyperpar[3]
  ID.sigma <- ID.precision^-0.5
  sample.IIDpred[, i] <- rnorm(nrow(pred), sd = ID.sigma)
}

x1 = pred_dummy[1:4] |> as.matrix()
x2 = pred_dummy[5:7] |> as.matrix()
x3 = pred_dummy[8:10] |> as.matrix()
x4 = pred$soil_moisture

linpred <-
  as.matrix(Ap %*% xSpace + as.matrix(
    cbind(
      1,
      x1,

x2,
      x3,
      x4

)
  ) %*% xX + sample.IIDpred)

inv.linpred <- gtools::inv.logit(linpred)

pred.grid <- data.frame(t(apply(inv.linpred, 1, FUN = function(x){ c(mean(x), sd(x), quantile(x, probs = c(0.025,0.5,0.975)))})))
colnames(pred.grid) <- c("mean", "sd", "0.025quant", "0.5quant", "0.975quant")
fitted.pred.mean <- pred.grid[["mean"]]
fitted.pred.sd     <- pred.grid[["sd"]]

quite complicated.

if you know the covariates where you want the new predictions, I would just
enlarge the model with those and turning the spde and rr off for those. then
you have them directly in the linear predictor

like

n <- 100
m <- 20

x <- rnorm(n)
xx <- rnorm(m)

y <- 1 + x + 0.2 * scale(arima.sim(n, model = list(ar = 0.9))) + rnorm(n)
yy <- rep(NA, m)

idx <- 1:n
iidx <- rep(NA, m)

model <- Y ~ 1 + X + f(IDX, model = "ar1")

data <- data.frame(Y = c(y, yy),
X = c(x, xx),
IDX = c(idx, iidx))

r <- inla(model, data = data, family = "stdnormal")
r$summary.linear.predictor[n + 1:m, "mean"]

## since iidx is NA, the AR1 term will be turned off.

## if your 'xx = x', then you do the same. much easier...

Dear Havard,

Based on the above explanation, I followed the method outlined below to obtain the mean prevalence from the posterior samples. What are your thoughts on this approach?

```

stk.e1 <- inla.stack(
  tag = 'point',
  data = list(y = dm$n, numtrials = dm$N),
  A = list(A, 1, 1),
  effects = list(
    s = indexs,
    rr = 1:length(dm$elevation_cat),  # Assuming all layers have the same length
    data.frame(
      b0 = 1,
      x1 = dm2$elevation_cat,
      x2 = dm2$improved_water_cat,
      x3 = dm2$open_def_cat,
      x4 = dm2$soil_moisture
    )
  )
)

stk.p1 <- inla.stack(
  tag = "pred",
  data = list(y = NA, numtrials = NA),
  A = list(Ap,1,1),
  effects = list(
    s = indexs,
    rr = (length(pred$elevation_cat) + 1):(length(pred$elevation_cat) + nrow(pred)),
    data.frame(
      b0 = 1,
      x1 = pred$elevation_cat,
      x2 = pred$improved_water_cat,
      x3 = pred$open_def_cat,
      x4 = pred$soil_moisture
    )
  )
)

formula <- y ~ 0 + b0 + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 +
  f(s, model = spde) +
  f(rr, model = 'iid', hyper = hyper.prec)

# stk.full has stk.e and stk.p
stk.full <- inla.stack(stk.e1, stk.p1)

#' The inla() call
mod <- inla(
  formula,
  family = "binomial",
  Ntrials = numtrials,
  data = inla.stack.data(stk.full),
  control.family = control.family(link = 'logit'),
  control.predictor = list(
    compute = TRUE,
    link = 1,
    A = inla.stack.A(stk.full)
  ),
  control.compute = list(config = TRUE, return.marginals.predictor = TRUE, cpo = T),
  control.inla = list(tolerance = 1e-7),
  num.threads = 7,
  verbose = F
)
index <- inla.stack.index(stack = stk.full, tag = "pred")$data
ps <- inla.posterior.sample(nsamp, mod, num.threads = 7, parallel.configs = T)
linpred = inla.posterior.sample.eval("APredictor", ps)[index, ]

inv.linpred <- gtools::inv.logit(linpred)
pred.grid <- data.frame(t(apply(
  inv.linpred,
  1,
  FUN = function(x) {
    c(mean(x), sd(x), quantile(x, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)))
  }
)))
colnames(pred.grid) <- c("mean", "sd", "0.025quant", "0.5quant", "0.975quant")
```

if you use control.predictor=list(A=...) then you have lin.pred in two layers

data depends on eta*

eta* = A %*% eta

eta is defined in the formula

then

APredictor = eta*

Predictor = eta

if 'A' is not used, then APredictor is NULL



What exactly do you want to do??? Normally, building the lin.predictor
